hypothesis: The assembled mechanism can be measured, inspected and reset repeatedly without hidden interference.
objective: Dimensional/clearance verification, datum survey, end-stop and sensor routing check.
output: Inspection report, clearance map, as-built configuration
criterion: No uncontrolled interference; all critical interfaces positively retained; deviations logged.

hypothesis: The intended translation DOF exists and is repeatable under manual/mechanical actuation.
objective: Demonstrate guided travel, lock states, stop engagement and reset.
load: Manual or controlled low-force actuation within safe envelope
output: Travel x(t), state sequence, interference observations
criterion: Continuous guided motion through intended envelope; no binding or unintended release.

hypothesis: The bilateral rails carry repeatable reactions without pathological load asymmetry caused by installation.
load: Incremental controlled load; exact ceiling set after fixture proof review
boundary: Base fixed; carriage constrained to intended DOF
criterion: Response is repeatable and within pre-approved fixture/load limits; unexplained asymmetry triggers inspection.

hypothesis: Each structurally relevant sliding/contact interface has a measurable configuration-specific friction law.
objective: Identify static/kinetic friction under P0 surface state.
load: Controlled normal preload and sliding motion
criterion: Repeatable identification with uncertainty and no fixture slip/secondary contact.

hypothesis: Mechanical stops/contact pairs have identifiable force-displacement behavior in the operating region.
load: Controlled compression/impact below fixture proof limit
criterion: Stable configuration-specific law with stated validity range; no extrapolated closure.

hypothesis: Mechanical contact damping is measurable and separable from structural compliance.
objective: Identify damping for selected contact pair.
criterion: Repeatable damping identification over tested range.

hypothesis: Restitution/rebound of the selected stop/contact pair is measurable and controllable.
objective: Identify rebound ratio versus approach condition.
load: Controlled impact velocities established by pre-test setup qualification
criterion: Valid runs free of fixture motion and secondary impacts.

hypothesis: The selected absorber cartridge produces a reproducible force-stroke relation.
objective: Measure F-x, hysteresis and end behavior.
load: Quasi-static and controlled dynamic profiles within verified fixture capacity
criterion: Curve traceable to exact cartridge serial/configuration; no generic curve substitution.

hypothesis: The absorber response depends measurably on stroke rate within the intended operating domain.
load: Defined rate sweep inside qualified equipment envelope
criterion: No fit used outside measured domain; repeatable trends.

hypothesis: Temperature alters absorber response and must be retained as a configuration variable where relevant.
load: Same mechanical profile at controlled temperatures
boundary: Thermal soak and safe temperature limits
criterion: Temperature state verified before each run; no inferred values between tested conditions without model disclosure.

hypothesis: Joint/fastener stiffness and preload measurably affect system compliance.
objective: Identify joint stiffness and preload sensitivity.
load: Controlled axial/shear excitation and preload states
criterion: Fixture compliance separated or quantified; exact fastener stack recorded.

hypothesis: Rotation-control joints have measurable clearance, friction and elastic compliance.
criterion: Repeatable joint map; left/right differences retained.

hypothesis: 170 can transition between intended mechanical states repeatedly without unintended release.
objective: Exercise normal -> armed/capture -> ride-down/release -> rebound/end states as implemented.
load: Controlled trigger/force/acceleration surrogate, not a crash pulse
boundary: Restraint path not relied upon for human safety; no occupant
output: State timeline, trigger threshold/latency, release cases
criterion: Intended transition repeatable; all unintended release/fault cases recorded.

hypothesis: The integrated carriage translates through the intended guided path without binding.
objective: Integrated low-load translation and stop test.
criterion: No binding/jam; stop engagement reproducible; any damage triggers teardown.

hypothesis: Seatback rotation-control remains mechanically distinct from longitudinal energy path.
objective: Test 150L/150R while longitudinal carriage motion is separately controlled/isolated.
boundary: Carriage locked for isolation test, then repeat with translation permitted
criterion: Measurable distinct reaction path and no unintended coupling beyond documented joint compliance.

hypothesis: The rebound-control module measurably limits reverse travel after primary translation.
load: Controlled release/return from bounded primary stroke
criterion: Reverse motion remains bounded and controlled; no uncontrolled return or secondary interference.

hypothesis: Changing one controlled design variable changes the measured mechanism response in the expected direction without confounding from other changes.
objective: A/B comparison using one-variable-at-a-time variant rule.
output: paired response metrics and effect estimate
criterion: Configuration, serial, setup and calibration matched; otherwise mark MULTIVARIABLE COMPARISON.

hypothesis: The integrated mechanism can repeat controlled dynamic events while preserving traceable state, force, displacement and rotation measurements.
objective: First integrated controlled dynamic screening; no occupant.
load: Laboratory-controlled dynamic excitation only; vehicle pulse is not assumed
boundary: Containment fixture, hard stops, safe load ceiling
output: full synchronized DAQ + video + post-test inspection
criterion: All channels valid, synchronization verified, no uncontrolled release, complete evidence package.

hypothesis: Post-test inspection can distinguish elastic recovery from permanent change and make the article reusable or sacrificial by rule.
objective: Teardown, dimensional reinspection, damage classification, reset decision.
output: damage map, permanent deformation, replacement decision
criterion: No reuse without documented inspection acceptance.
